findings.issue_text: [High/security] The `except Integration.DoesNotExist` path advances without verifying that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user owns or administers the supplied installation ID, allowing an attacker to race webhook processing or use a known installation ID to link another user's GitHub App installation to their Sentry organization.

goldens.comment: Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing

The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] The `except Integration.DoesNotExist` path advances without verifying that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user owns or administers the supplied installation ID, allowing an attacker to race webhook processing or use a known installation ID to link another user's GitHub App installation to their Sentry organization.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a security issue. Looking at the diff in GitHubInstallation.dispatch(), when Integration.DoesNotExist is caught (lines 487-488), the code simply calls `return pipeline.next_step()` without any verification that the authenticated GitHub user has any relationship to the installation_id. The OAuth verification (checking github_authenticated_user against integration.metadata['sender']['login']) only happens in the else branch when the Integration already exists (lines 495-502). This means for new installations, an attacker could potentially use any installation_id to proceed through the pipeline without proving ownership.
